mainTopic: A student ruling during his רב's lifetime or in his presence: the תלמיד חבר exception, checking a שחיטה knife, stopping an איסור, and the punishments for ruling before one's רב
overview: This amud deals with a student who gives halachic rulings (הוראה) while his רב is alive or present. רבינא checked a שחיטה knife, and he defends himself by saying he is רב אשי's תלמיד חבר, just as רב המנונא was to רב חסדא. רבא rules that a צורבא מרבנן may check a knife for himself, and two stories test that rule. In one, רבינא sends his host's knife to רבא because he is only buying the meat. In the other, רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא is punished for checking a knife in רב אחא בר יעקב's town. רבא adds that a student may speak up even in front of his רב to stop an איסור, because where there is חילול השם the רב's honor is set aside. He then says that ruling in the רב's presence carries מיתה, while ruling away from him is only forbidden, and the גמרא defends this against the story of יהודה בן גוריא. The amud ends with a series of teachings on how severe it is to rule before one's רב: a snake bite, being called a חוטא, אלעזר הכהן being lowered from his greatness, and dying childless. Along the way there is a side teaching that giving all one's priestly gifts to one כהן brings famine.

steps.title: רב המנונא ruled in חרתא דארגז while רב חסדא was alive
steps.stepSummary: A report that רב המנונא gave halachic rulings in the town of חרתא דארגז during רב חסדא's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא gave halachic rulings in חרתא דארגז during the years of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a historical fact: רב המנונא gave rulings while רב חסדא, who taught him, was still alive. This fact will be used as evidence in the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a student may not give הוראה while his teacher is alive. This report suggests there are exceptions, and the גמרא will soon explain why רב המנונא was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave a halachic ruling (from הוֹרָאָה)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna gave halachic rulings
in Charta d'Argez
during the years (lifetime) of Rav Chisda.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא was one of his teachers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the larger discussion on the daf about a student ruling in front of, or during the lifetime of, his teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב המנונא ruled during רב חסדא's lifetime.

steps.title: רבינא checks a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רבינא examined a שחיטה knife in בבל while רב אשי, his teacher, was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא examined a slaughtering knife in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a story. רבינא checked a knife for שחיטה, which counts as giving a halachic ruling. The next steps will challenge this action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking the knife counts as הוראה, since it decides whether the knife is fit for שחיטה. רב אשי, רבינא's teacher, also lived in בבל, so the question is whether this was allowed.

phrases.english: Ravina examined a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia.
phrases.notes: Checking a knife is a form of halachic ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a practical case where the precedent of רב המנונא will be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא acted as a halachic decisor by checking a knife during רב אשי's lifetime.

steps.title: רב אשי asks רבינא why he did this
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבינא: how could you rule while I, your teacher, am alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: What is the reason the Master acted this way?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a question that is really a challenge. A student is not supposed to rule during his teacher's lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words sound like a polite question (מאי טעמא), but they work as an objection. רבינא now has to justify what he did.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
What is the reason the Master acted this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's action from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's checking of the knife during רב אשי's lifetime
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A student may not give הוראה while his teacher is alive, and רב אשי is רבינא's teacher.

steps.title: רבינא cites רב המנונא as precedent
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רב המנונא ruled during רב חסדא's lifetime, so he may do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't רב המנונא give rulings in חרתא דארגז during the years of רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself by pointing to the precedent from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's argument is: if רב המנונא could rule during his teacher's life, so can I. The question now becomes whether that report about רב המנונא is accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (introduces a proof)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא רַב הַמְנוּנָא אוֹרִי
phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't Rav Hamnuna give rulings
in Charta d'Argez during the years of Rav Chisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge by bringing the precedent from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: A student may rule during his teacher's lifetime
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report that רב המנונא ruled during רב חסדא's lifetime

steps.title: רב אשי says the report was that רב המנונא did not rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof: the correct tradition is that רב המנונא did NOT rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was stated 'he did not rule.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבינא's proof. He says the correct version of the report is the opposite: רב המנונא did not rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not argue with רבינא's logic. He attacks the factual basis of the proof. If רב המנונא never ruled, רבינא has no precedent.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was stated 'he did NOT rule.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The factual basis of the precedent
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tradition about רב המנונא was reported wrongly. He actually did not rule.

steps.title: Both reports are true: no rulings under רב הונא, rulings under רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reconciles the two traditions. רב המנונא did not rule while רב הונא, his main teacher, was alive. He did rule while רב חסדא was alive, because he was רב חסדא's תלמיד חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was stated 'he ruled,' and it was stated 'he did not rule.' During the years of רב הונא, his teacher, he did not rule. He did rule during the years of רב חסדא, because he was his student-colleague.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that both versions are correct. Each one refers to a different teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on ruling applies to a student's main teacher (רבו מובהק), here רב הונא. For a תלמיד חבר, a student who is also nearly a colleague, ruling is allowed. That was רב המנונא's relationship with רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: A student who is also a colleague

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two reports contradict each other. One is about רב הונא and the other is about רב חסדא, two different teachers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates the key distinction: the ban on הוראה applies to one's main teacher, not to a teacher for whom one is a תלמיד חבר.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was stated 'he ruled,'
and it was stated 'he did not rule.'
During the years of Rav Huna, his teacher,
that is when he did not rule,
but he did rule during the years of Rav Chisda,
since he was his student-colleague.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's rejection by showing that both traditions exist and fit together.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different teachers, different relationships
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports contradict each other, so one must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are true. He did not rule under his main teacher רב הונא, but he ruled under רב חסדא, for whom he was a תלמיד חבר.

steps.title: רבינא is also רב אשי's student-colleague
steps.stepSummary: רבינא applies the rule to himself: he is רב אשי's תלמיד חבר, so he may rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I, too, am the Master's student-colleague.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his defense by applying the תלמיד חבר rule to his own relationship with רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבינא is to רב אשי what רב המנונא was to רב חסדא, the same permission applies. That justifies his checking the knife.
steps.whatToRemember: A student may not rule during the lifetime of his main teacher. A תלמיד חבר, a student who is also a colleague, may rule. Like רב המנונא with רב חסדא, רבינא was a תלמיד חבר of רב אשי.

phrases.english: And I, too, am a student-colleague
of the Master.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנָא נָמֵי תַּלְמִיד חָבֵר דְּמָר אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the distinction from step 6 to רבינא's own case, answering רב אשי's challenge from step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: As רב אשי's תלמיד חבר, רבינא was allowed to check the knife.

steps.title: A Torah scholar may check a knife for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a צורבא מרבנן may examine a שחיטה knife for his own use without showing it to the local חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A young Torah scholar may examine the knife for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבא. A Torah scholar may check his own slaughtering knife without bringing it to the town's רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, people showed their שחיטה knife to the local חכם out of respect for his authority. This connects to the earlier discussion about not ruling in a teacher's place. רבא says that checking a knife for your own use is not 'ruling' in the רב's place, so a scholar may do it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A young Torah scholar (literally, someone 'heated up' by the rabbis' learning)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the stories that follow. Each story tests exactly when it applies.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A Torah scholar may examine [a knife] for himself.
phrases.notes: This means for his own slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן חָזֵי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules about ruling in a teacher's presence to a related case: checking a שחיטה knife in a חכם's town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורבא מרבנן may examine a knife for his own use without showing it to the local חכם.

steps.title: רבינא sends his host's knife to רבא
steps.stepSummary: In מחוזא, רבא's town, רבינא's host shows him a knife. רבינא tells him to take it to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came to מחוזא. His host brought a knife and showed it to him. רבינא said to him: Go take it to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a question. רבינא, a scholar, refuses to check the knife himself and sends it to רבא instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוזא was רבא's town, so רבא was the local authority there. רבינא's behavior seems to go against רבא's own rule from Step 8. That tension is what the next step will raise.

phrases.english: Ravina happened to come to Meḥoza,
phrases.notes: מחוזא was רבא's town.

phrases.english: his host brought out a knife
and showed it to him.
He said to him: Go, bring it to Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case that seems to clash with רבא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא sends the host's knife to the local חכם, רבא, instead of checking it himself.

steps.title: The host asks why רבינא doesn't rely on רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The host challenges רבינא: doesn't he hold of רבא's rule that a scholar may check a knife for himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: The host said to him: Doesn't the master hold of what רבא said, that a Torah scholar may examine a knife for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The host questions רבינא's behavior. Since רבינא is a scholar, why can't he check the knife himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The host is slaughtering the animal for רבינא, so in his eyes this counts as 'for himself.' If so, רבא's rule should let רבינא check the knife and skip bothering רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master hold…? (a way of asking someone to explain himself)

phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
that which Rava said:
A Torah scholar may examine [a knife] for himself?
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רבא's rule here as the basis of the host's challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר מָר הָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's rule (Step 8) to challenge רבינא's action (Step 9).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's refusal to examine the knife himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא allows a scholar to check a knife for himself. The meat is for רבינא, so he should be allowed to check it.

steps.title: רבינא explains that he is only a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that he is only buying the meat from the host, so this is not 'for himself.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: I am just buying [the meat] from you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the host's challenge. He is not the one doing the slaughtering. He is only buying meat, so רבא's rule does not cover him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule applies only when the scholar is the one using the knife. Here the host is the slaughterer, and רבינא is just a customer. So the knife still needs to go to the local חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: I am merely buying (a doubled verb that stresses 'only buying')

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule lets a scholar check a knife only for his own slaughtering. A scholar who is just receiving or buying the meat must still send the knife to the local חכם.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the host's slaughtering 'for רבינא' counts as רבינא slaughtering for himself. רבינא is only the buyer, so the leniency does not apply.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am merely buying [it from you].
phrases.notes: The doubled verb stresses that he is only a buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the host's challenge by limiting the scope of רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (distinguishing the case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the meat is being prepared for רבינא, he counts as checking 'for himself.'
steps.terutzMaskana: A buyer is not the user of the knife, so רבא's leniency does not apply to him.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן to help remember the names of the חכמים in the next story.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: זילא להניא, מחליף, איקא, and יעקב.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא is setting up the next story by giving a memory aid for the names that will appear in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word hints at one person: זילא להניא stands for רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא, מחליף for רב אבא בר תחליפא, איקא for רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, and יעקב for רב אחא בר יעקב. The גמרא was once learned by heart, so memory aids like this were very helpful.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint for רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא
A hint for רב אבא בר תחליפא

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Zila Lehanya,
phrases.notes: Hints at רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא.

phrases.english: Maḥlif, Ika, and Ya'akov.)
phrases.notes: Hints at רב אבא בר תחליפא, רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, and רב אחא בר יעקב.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: זִילָא לְהַנְיָא, מַחְלִיף, אִיקָא, וְיַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that introduces the next story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a memory aid for the names in the next story.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא shows his guests a knife
steps.stepSummary: Two חכמים visit רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, in the town where רב אחא בר יעקב is the authority. He wants to slaughter a choice calf for them and shows them the knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא and רב אבא בר תחליפא visited the house of רב אחא son of רב איקא, in the area of רב אחא בר יעקב. רב אחא son of רב איקא wanted to make them a third-born calf, so he brought a knife and showed it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second knife story. This step sets up the next move: what the visitors will do with the knife in another חכם's town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that this town belongs to רב אחא בר יעקב, so he is the local authority. The visiting scholars are being asked to check a knife in his territory. This is like רבינא in רבא's town, and the reader should wait for their response next.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place (the area where a חכם has authority)
A third-born calf, considered a delicacy (some explain: a calf that reached a third of its growth)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar from Hagronya
and Rav Abba bar Taḥalifa

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא,
phrases.english: happened to come to the house of Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika,
in the place [of authority] of Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov.
phrases.notes: This is the key detail: another חכם is the local authority here.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, wanted
to prepare for them a third-born calf,
he brought a knife and showed it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא וְרַב אַבָּא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא אִיקְּלַעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the second story, which was introduced by the סימן. It is another test of checking a knife in a local חכם's town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is the setup: visiting scholars are shown a knife in רב אחא בר יעקב's town.

steps.title: Should we not respect the Elder?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר תחליפא suggests that they bring the knife to the elder, רב אחא בר יעקב, out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר תחליפא said to them: Should we not be concerned about the honor of the Elder?
steps.whatsHappening: One of the two guests raises a concern. This is his town's senior scholar, so maybe they should show him the knife instead of checking it themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The Elder" is רב אחא בר יעקב, the authority in this town (Step 13). Checking a knife works like giving a halachic ruling. Doing it yourself in a great scholar's town could look like you are ignoring him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Elder, here meaning רב אחא בר יעקב
not, used here as a question: should we not?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַחָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Tachlifa said to them:
Should we not be concerned for the Elder?
phrases.notes: Meaning: for his honor. We should bring the knife to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 13. The knife has just been shown to the guests.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should the knife be brought to the local elder out of respect, instead of being checked by the guests?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר cites רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא answers that רבא allows a Torah scholar to check a knife for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא said to them: This is what רבא said: A young Torah scholar may examine a knife for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The second guest answers the concern. He quotes רבא's rule that a scholar may check a knife for his own use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule of רבא that came up in the רבינא story (Step 10). רבי אלעזר thinks the rule settles the matter. The guests are eating the meat themselves, so they do not need the local authority.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar from Hagronya said to them:
This is what Rava said:
A young Torah scholar may examine for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the concern raised in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no need to go to the elder, because רבא allows a scholar to check a knife for himself.

steps.title: He checked the knife and was punished
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא checked the knife himself and was punished for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He examined it, and רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא was punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי אלעזר went ahead and checked the knife, and he was punished from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment shows that he was wrong to skip the elder. This seems to clash with רבא's rule, and that sets up the question in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבא's rule is wrong. The גמרא will explain why this case was different.

phrases.english: He examined it,
and Rabbi Elazar from Hagronya was punished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of acting on the answer in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking the knife in this situation led to punishment.

steps.title: But רבא allowed it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he was punished, since רבא permits a scholar to check for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: A young Torah scholar may examine for himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the punishment. רבי אלעזר simply followed רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule allows a scholar to check his own knife, he did nothing wrong. So why was he punished?

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (a formula for a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
A young Torah scholar may examine for himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the punishment in Step 16, using the rule quoted in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The punishment of רבי אלעזר מהגרוניא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He acted according to רבא's rule, so a punishment seems unjustified.

steps.title: They had already raised his honor
steps.stepSummary: This case was different, because they had already begun talking about the elder's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because they had begun discussing his honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. Once רב אחא בר תחליפא mentioned the elder's honor, ignoring it became disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule still holds in an ordinary case. But here the honor of רב אחא בר יעקב had been openly brought up. Going ahead anyway showed disrespect, and that is why he was punished.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because they had begun with his honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (an exception to the rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's rule allows checking for oneself in every situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the elder's honor has been mentioned, a scholar must defer to him.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב was exceptionally great
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב אחא בר יעקב was outstanding, so he deserved extra honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: רב אחא בר יעקב is different, because he was outstanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer. רבא's rule does not apply in the town of a scholar as great as רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the exception depends on who the authority was, not on what was said. A truly outstanding elder must be deferred to even if nobody mentions him.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introduces a second answer)
outstanding, distinguished in age and wisdom

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule that a scholar may check a knife for himself still stands. It gives way when the local authority's honor is raised, or when he is exceptionally great.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rav Acha bar Yaakov is different,
because he was outstanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by the stature of the authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any local scholar's presence still leaves room for רבא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the town of an exceptionally great elder, one must defer to him.

steps.title: To stop an איסור, one may rule even before his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a student may speak out against an איסור even in his teacher's presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And to separate someone from a prohibition, even in his teacher's presence it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to the rule against ruling in front of your teacher. If someone is about to do an איסור, you may stop him right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, giving a ruling in front of your רבי is disrespectful. But preventing a sin comes first. Stopping someone from transgressing is not seen as taking your teacher's place.

keyTerms.meaning: to separate someone from a prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit on the honor owed to a teacher: it never prevents stopping a sin.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And to separate someone from a prohibition —
even in his presence, it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from honoring a local authority to a new rule about ruling in front of one's teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To prevent an איסור, a student may rule even in his teacher's presence.

steps.title: רבינא sees a man tie his donkey to a tree on שבת
steps.stepSummary: While sitting before רב אשי, רבינא sees a man tying his donkey to a palm tree on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting before רב אשי. He saw a certain man tying his donkey to a palm tree on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that relates to רבא's rule. It is setting up a case where an איסור happens in front of a teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tree on שבת is forbidden by a rabbinic decree. רבינא is in front of his teacher רב אשי, so the question is whether he may protest.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Ravina was sitting before Rav Ashi,
he saw a certain man
who was tying his donkey
to a palm tree on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that illustrates רבא's rule from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case of an איסור happening in front of a teacher.

steps.title: רבינא declares the man excommunicated
steps.stepSummary: The man ignores רבינא's shout, so רבינא declares that he should be in שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised his voice at him, but the man paid no attention. He said to him: Let this man be in excommunication.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא protests, but the man ignores him. So רבינא declares, in front of רב אשי, that the man should be put in שמתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא is acting on the idea of stopping an איסור even before his teacher. Declaring a שמתא is a strong step. The story continues next with whether doing this in front of רב אשי was proper.

phrases.english: He raised his voice at him,
but he paid no attention to him.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: Following the reference translation, he said this to רב אשי.

phrases.english: Let this man be in excommunication.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 21 with רבינא's response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא places the man in שמתא for ignoring his rebuke.

steps.title: רבינא asks if his outburst was disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether shouting out and putting a man in שמתא in front of his teacher looked like disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: When I act like this, does it look like disrespect toward you?
steps.whatsHappening: After the incident with the donkey, רבינא worries that he acted disrespectfully in front of his teacher. He asks רב אשי about it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a student should not issue rulings or punishments in front of his רב. רבינא just did exactly that by declaring שמתא. So he asks whether his act counts as אפקרותא, meaning disrespect.

phrases.english: He (Ravina) said to him (Rav Ashi): Something like this,
phrases.notes: Refers to the shout and the שמתא from the previous steps.

phrases.english: does it appear like disrespect?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא, מִי מִתְחֲזֵא כְּאַפְקֵרוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבינא's declaration of שמתא in front of רב אשי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether acting against a sinner in the רב's presence counts as disrespect to the רב.

steps.title: No honor for the teacher when God's name is desecrated
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with a פסוק: where there is חילול השם, the respect normally owed to a רב is set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: 'There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel against ה׳.' Wherever there is a חילול השם, we do not give honor to the teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי reassures רבינא that he acted correctly. When God's honor is at stake, the teacher's honor steps aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that no human wisdom, not even a great רב's, stands against God's honor. So stopping a public שבת violation comes before the usual etiquette of not ruling in the רב's presence. This confirms what רבא taught in Step 20.

keyTerms.term: אֵין חׇכְמָה וְאֵין תְּבוּנָה וְאֵין עֵצָה לְנֶגֶד ה׳
keyTerms.meaning: No wisdom, understanding, or counsel stands against ה׳‎ (משלי כ״א:ל׳)
We do not give honor to the teacher

steps.whatToRemember: When a חילול השם is happening, a student must speak up even in front of his רב. The רב's honor does not hold him back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that כבוד הרב is set aside to prevent a חילול השם.

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him: "There is no wisdom and no understanding
and no counsel against ה׳" (Proverbs 21:30),

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם —
phrases.english: any place where there is a desecration of God's name,
we do not give honor to the teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם אֵין חוֹלְקִין כָּבוֹד לָרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is not disrespect. Where there is חילול השם, the רב's honor is set aside.

steps.title: רבא distinguishes ruling in the teacher's presence and away from him
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a student who rules halacha in front of his רב is forbidden and liable to death. If he rules away from the רב, it is forbidden but there is no death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In his presence, it is forbidden and he is liable to death. Not in his presence, it is forbidden but he is not liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבא's general rule for a student who rules halacha in his teacher's area, in a normal case where he is not stopping an איסור. There are two levels of severity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are forbidden. The difference is only the punishment. Ruling right in front of the רב brings מיתה בידי שמים, which is death at the hands of Heaven. Ruling in his area but not in front of him is only a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to death (here: at the hands of Heaven)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different case from Steps 20–24. There the student spoke up to stop an איסור, which is allowed. Here רבא is talking about an ordinary halachic ruling with no איסור to prevent.

phrases.english: Rava said: In his presence, it is forbidden,
and he is liable to death.
Not in his presence, it is forbidden,
but he is not liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּפָנָיו אָסוּר וְחַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exception (stopping an איסור) to the basic rule about ruling near one's רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ruling in the רב's presence is forbidden and carries death. Ruling away from him is forbidden but carries no death penalty.

steps.title: Challenge from the death of Aaron's sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבא's claim that there is no death penalty away from the רב. It begins quoting a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says בני אהרן died for ruling halacha before משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not in his presence, he is not liable? But it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, the sons of אהרן died only because they ruled halacha in front of משה their teacher. What did they expound? 'And the sons of אהרן the כהן shall put fire on the altar.' They said: Even though fire comes down from heaven, it is a מצוה to bring ordinary fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an attack on the second half of רבא's rule. It quotes a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר. This step is setting up the challenge, and the sharp point will come at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows how serious ruling before one's רב is. נדב and אביהוא made a real דרשה from a פסוק, yet they died for ruling in front of משה. The ברייתא goes on to tell of רבי אליעזר's student. The real challenge to רבא comes when רבה בר בר חנה adds a detail about that student.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא), introducing a challenge
The sons of אהרן (נדב and אביהוא)

steps.confusionAlert: The story of בני אהרן itself happened בפניו, in משה's presence, so it matches רבא's rule. Even the ברייתא's student story says he ruled 'בפניו'. The actual problem for רבא comes from רבה בר בר חנה's added detail (step 29) that the student was three פרסאות away.

phrases.english: And not in his presence, he is not (liable to death)?
But it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The sons of Aaron did not die

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהוֹרוּ הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבָּן.
phrases.english: except because they ruled halacha before Moses their teacher.
What did they expound?
"And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put
fire on the altar" (Leviticus 1:7),

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָאֵשׁ יוֹרֶדֶת מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: they said: Even though fire comes down from heaven,
it is a מצוה to bring ordinary fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבא's rule from Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that ruling שלא בפניו carries no death penalty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records deaths for ruling before a רב, including a student of רבי אליעזר. רבה בר בר חנה later adds, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that this student was three פרסאות away. That detail suggests a death penalty even שלא בפניו.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's student who ruled and died
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a student ruled halacha before רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר predicted to his wife אימא שלום that the student would not live out the year, and he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר had a student who ruled halacha in his presence. רבי אליעזר said to his wife אימא שלום: I will be surprised if this one lives out his year. And he did not live out his year.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a second story, this time from רבי אליעזר's own life. The גמרא is still building its challenge, and the decisive detail about the student will come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that death for ruling before a רב really happens, even in a later generation. Soon the גמרא will add that this student was actually three פרסאות away from רבי אליעזר. That would mean death even שלא בפניו, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: I am surprised / I would wonder
Will complete his year (will live until year's end)

phrases.aramaic: וְתַלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer had a certain student,
who ruled halacha in his presence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְאִימָּא שָׁלוֹם אִשְׁתּוֹ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Imma Shalom, his wife:

phrases.aramaic: תָּמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יוֹצִיא זֶה שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: I will be surprised if this one completes his year.
And he did not complete his year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר שֶׁהוֹרָה הֲלָכָה בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 26 as part of the same challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that there is no death penalty שלא בפניו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The student died for his ruling. The coming detail that he was three פרסאות away will show death even away from the רב.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר explains his prediction to his wife
steps.stepSummary: אימא שלום asks רבי אליעזר if he is a נביא. He says no, he simply has a קבלה: whoever rules halacha in front of his רב is חייב מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Are you a prophet? He said to her: I am not a prophet, and I am not the son of a prophet. Rather, this is what I received from my teachers: anyone who rules halacha in front of his teacher is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא we started quoting continues. רבי אליעזר explains that his prediction came from a received tradition, not from prophecy. This is still the build-up of the challenge against רבא. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife assumed only a נביא could know a person would die within the year. רבי אליעזר says it is simply the halacha: ruling before one's רב carries a death penalty from שמים. This sets up the question of whether this student was actually 'in front of' his רב.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received (a tradition from my teachers)
Liable to death (here, a death penalty from Heaven)

phrases.english: She said to him: Are you a prophet?
phrases.notes: His wife, אימא שלום, is surprised that his prediction came true.

phrases.english: He said to her: I am not a prophet
phrases.notes: The wording echoes the words of the prophet עמוס (עמוס ז:יד).

phrases.english: and I am not the son of a prophet,
rather, this is what I have received:
phrases.notes: This is a tradition passed down from his teachers.

phrases.english: anyone who rules halacha in front of his teacher
is liable to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 26-27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 25) that there is no death penalty when the student rules away from his רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the source material for the attack. The ברייתא confirms that the student's death was a punishment for ruling before his רב. The next step adds that he was actually far away.

steps.title: The student was three parasangs away
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: the student was יהודה בן גוריא, and he was three פרסאות away from רבי אליעזר. So he died even though he ruled far from his רב, which contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That student's name was יהודה בן גוריא, and he was three parasangs away from him! (So how can רבא say there is no death penalty when the student is away from his teacher?)
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch of the challenge against רבא. The student who died was not near רבי אליעזר. He was three פרסאות away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that ruling away from one's רב is forbidden but carries no death penalty. Here a student ruled far away and still died. That looks like a direct contradiction to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs, a Persian unit of distance (about 4 מיל each)
The name of the student who died

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד יְהוּדָה בֶּן גּוּרְיָא שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: that student's name was Yehuda ben Gurya,
and he was three parasangs away from him?!
phrases.notes: The question mark shows this is a challenge against רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the decisive detail that turns the ברייתא into a challenge against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא: ruling away from one's רב carries no death penalty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יהודה בן גוריא was three פרסאות away and still died. So even ruling away from the רב seems to carry a death penalty.

steps.title: The ruling was actually in his presence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ruling took place in front of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the student actually ruled in front of רבי אליעזר, so the case fits רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling happened in front of the רב, the death penalty matches exactly what רבא said. The three פרסאות must then mean something else, such as where the student usually lived.

phrases.english: It was in his presence.
phrases.notes: The distance refers to the student's usual place, not where he stood when he ruled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ruling itself happened in front of the רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The student ruled from three פרסאות away and died for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The student ruled in front of רבי אליעזר. So רבא's rule stands.

steps.title: But he said three parasangs away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבה בר בר חנה explicitly said the student was three פרסאות away!
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'three parasangs away from him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The quote clearly mentions a distance, so how can we say the student was in front of his רב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would רבה בר בר חנה mention the distance unless it explains what happened? The natural reading is that the distance is part of the case. That seems to undo the answer of step 30.

phrases.english: But behold, 'far from him'
three parasangs, he says!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רָחוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ פַּרְסָאוֹת קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ruling happened in front of the רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A detail mentioned in a story should matter to the story. So the distance should describe where the student was when he ruled.

steps.title: Details were given so it would not seem like a parable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: by your logic, why mention his name and his father's name? Those details were given only so we would not think the story was a parable. The distance detail serves the same purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, why mention his name and his father's name? Rather, it was so that you should not say it was a parable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that not every detail in the story is legally relevant. Some details are there just to show the story really happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name יהודה בן גוריא has nothing to do with the halacha. It was mentioned to prove that this was a real event. The three פרסאות works the same way: it describes where the student lived, so the answer 'בפניו הוה' stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the challenger's logic back on him)
A parable, a made-up story used to teach a lesson

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule stands. The death penalty applies when a student rules in front of his רב. The story of יהודה בן גוריא happened in front of רבי אליעזר. The extra details only show that the story is real.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
why mention his name and his father's name?
Rather, so that you should not say it was a parable.
phrases.notes: The distance detail is explained the same way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 and confirms the answer of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that a detail is not legally relevant: it only shows the story is real.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every detail in the story, including the distance, describes the legal case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Details like the name and the distance only show this was a real event, not a parable. The ruling happened in front of the רב.

steps.title: Ruling before one's teacher deserves a snake bite
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: whoever rules halacha before his רב deserves to be bitten by a snake. This is learned by linking זחלתי (אליהוא) with זוחלי עפר (snakes).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who rules הלכה in front of his teacher deserves to be bitten by a snake. As it says: 'And אליהוא son of ברכאל the בוזי answered and said: I am young in days... therefore I held back (זחלתי).' And it is written: 'With the venom of the crawlers (זוחלי) of the dust.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on the same topic. It describes the punishment for ruling before one's רב as being bitten by a snake, and gives a source from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהוא was younger than איוב's friends and hesitated to speak, saying 'זחלתי.' The same root appears in 'זוחלי עפר,' which means snakes. So אליהוא was saying: I was afraid, because one who speaks before his elders deserves a snake's bite.

keyTerms.meaning: That a snake should bite him
I held back / I was afraid (from the root ז-ח-ל)
Crawlers of the dust, meaning snakes
The young speaker in ספר איוב who waited for his elders to speak first

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds another layer to how serious it is for a student to rule before his רב. The danger is described as a snake bite, matching the root that אליהוא used when he hesitated to speak.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
anyone who rules halacha in front of his teacher
deserves to be bitten by a snake,
as it says: 'And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered'
phrases.notes: איוב לב:ו.

phrases.english: and said: I am young in days, etc.
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'and you are very old.'

phrases.english: therefore I held back (zachalti).'
phrases.notes: This is the key word, from the root ז-ח-ל.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'With the venom of the crawlers of the dust.'
phrases.notes: דברים לב:כד. The same root here refers to snakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כׇּל הַמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of ruling before one's רב with a new teaching from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rules halacha before his רב deserves to be bitten by a snake. This is derived from the shared root ז-ח-ל in זחלתי and זוחלי עפר.

steps.title: One who rules before his teacher is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: זעירי quotes רבי חנינא: a student who rules halacha in front of his רב is called a חוטא. The source is the פסוק 'בלבי צפנתי אמרתך למען לא אחטא לך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: he is called a sinner, as it says: 'I have hidden Your word in my heart, so that I will not sin against You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more opinion about a student who rules in front of his רב: he is called a sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד says he kept God's word hidden inside his heart so he would not sin. Saying Torah out loud is normally a good thing, so it can only be a sin in a special case. That case is ruling in front of one's רב.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not say that teaching Torah is a sin. The sin is only speaking up in front of one's רב.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
he is called a sinner,
phrases.notes: Refers to one who rules halacha in front of his teacher.

phrases.english: as it says: 'In my heart I have hidden Your word'
so that I will not sin against You.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קיט:יא

steps.triggerLanguage: זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another consequence for ruling before one's רב, after רבי יוחנן's snake-bite statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rules halacha before his רב is labeled a חוטא.

steps.title: Contradiction between two verses of David
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא points out a contradiction. In one פסוק דוד hid Torah in his heart, but in another he proclaimed righteousness in a great congregation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא pointed out a contradiction: It is written 'In my heart I have hidden Your word,' and it is written 'I proclaimed righteousness in a great congregation'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא sets two פסוקים against each other. One says דוד kept Torah to himself, and the other says he taught it publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק sounds like דוד stayed silent. The second sounds like he spoke Torah openly to crowds. Both cannot be true at the same time without some explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'In my heart I have hidden Your word,'
and it is written: 'I proclaimed righteousness in a great congregation'!
phrases.notes: תהלים מ:י

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the פסוק from step 34 fits with another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בלבי צפנתי אמרתך' as דוד keeping silent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second פסוק shows דוד teaching openly. That contradicts the idea that he hid his Torah.

steps.title: Silent while his teacher lived, public after
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים describe different times. While עירא היאירי, דוד's רב, was alive, דוד kept quiet. After he died, דוד taught publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here, it is when עירא היאירי was alive; there, it is when עירא היאירי was no longer alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא resolves the contradiction by assigning each פסוק to a different time in דוד's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד hid his Torah only out of respect for his living רב. Once his רב was gone, there was no problem, so he taught openly. This fits the rule that one should not rule in front of one's רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the contradiction can be resolved)

steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that the restriction exists only while the רב is alive. It also brings up עירא היאירי, which leads into the next teaching.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here — when Ira HaYa'iri was alive,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין עִירָא הַיָּאִירִי קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there — when Ira HaYa'iri was no longer alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 35.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים describe דוד's behavior in the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד was silent while his רב lived and spoke publicly after his רב's death.

steps.title: Giving all gifts to one priest brings famine
steps.stepSummary: Since עירא היאירי was mentioned, the גמרא brings a side teaching. רבי אבא בר זבדא says that giving all one's priestly gifts to one כהן brings famine, citing 'עירא היאירי היה כהן לדוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא said: Whoever gives his gifts to one כהן brings famine to the world, as it says: 'עירא היאירי was a כהן for דוד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside to a related teaching about עירא היאירי. It quotes a rule and the פסוק it is based on, and the next step will explain how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The priestly gifts (מתנות כהונה) should be spread among כהנים. Giving them all to one כהן is wrong and brings punishment. The proof comes from how the פסוק describes עירא היאירי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said:
Whoever gives his priestly gifts to one priest,
brings famine to the world,
as it says: 'Ira HaYa'iri was a priest for David.'
phrases.notes: שמואל II 20:26

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן מַתְּנוֹתָיו לְכֹהֵן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A tangent triggered by the mention of עירא היאירי in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving all one's priestly gifts to a single כהן brings famine.

steps.title: Was he a priest only for David?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the plain wording of the פסוק. Was עירא a כהן only for דוד and not for everyone else?
steps.simpleTranslation: Was he a כהן only for דוד, and not for the whole world?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the words 'a כהן for דוד' sound strange. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן serves all of כלל ישראל, not just one person. So the phrase 'כהן לדוד' must be hinting at something special between עירא and דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: For everyone else (literally 'for the whole world')

phrases.english: Was it only for David that he was a priest,
and not for everyone else?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדָוִד הוּא דַּהֲוָה כֹּהֵן, לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק cited in step 37, to show how it proves the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal meaning of 'היה כהן לדוד'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן is not the private כהן of one person, so the literal reading makes no sense.

steps.title: David sent all his gifts to Ira, and famine followed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means דוד sent all his priestly gifts to עירא alone. The very next פסוק says there was a famine in דוד's days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that דוד would send him all his gifts. And it is written right after: 'There was a famine in the days of דוד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the strange wording: עירא was 'דוד's כהן' because he got all of דוד's gifts. The famine described right afterward is the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כהן לדוד' means the one כהן who received all of דוד's gifts. The next פסוק reports a famine, which links the famine to this practice. That completes רבי אבא בר זבדא's proof.
steps.whatToRemember: Priestly gifts should be spread among many כהנים. Giving them all to one כהן is seen as harmful, as learned from דוד and עירא היאירי.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that David would send him his gifts,
and it is written right after it:
'And there was a famine in the days of David.'
phrases.notes: שמואל II 21:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38 and completes the proof for step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Non-literal reading of the פסוק plus proof from the following פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כהן לדוד' would mean he served only דוד, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד gave all his gifts to עירא, and the famine came right after.

steps.title: One who rules before his teacher is lowered from greatness
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the main topic, רבי אליעזר says one who rules in front of his רב is lowered from his greatness. The proof is אלעזר הכהן, who taught the soldiers a law in front of משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: We lower him from his greatness, as it says: 'And אלעזר הכהן said to the men of the army, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of ruling before one's רב. It brings רבי אליעזר's view that such a person loses his high position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלעזר taught the laws of koshering vessels (הגעלה) to the soldiers while משה, his רב, was present. That is ruling in front of one's רב, and the punishment is a loss of stature.

keyTerms.meaning: We lower / he is brought down

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
he is lowered from his greatness,
phrases.notes: Refers to one who rules in front of his teacher.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And Elazar the priest said'
to the men of the army, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר לא:כא

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מוֹרִידִין אוֹתוֹ מִגְּדוּלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the עירא היאירי tangent to the main topic of ruling before one's רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rules before his רב is lowered from his position of greatness.

steps.title: Even crediting משה did not save Elazar
steps.stepSummary: Even though אלעזר said the law was commanded to his uncle משה and not to him, he was still punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he told them: 'He commanded my father's brother, and He did not command me,' even so he was punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stresses how strict the rule is. Even giving credit to משה did not protect אלעזר from punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think quoting your רב's teaching is allowed, since you are not claiming it as your own. Yet אלעזר was punished even though he credited משה. The problem was speaking up as the authority while his רב was present.

keyTerms.meaning: To my father's brother (משה, אלעזר's uncle)

steps.whatToRemember: Ruling in front of one's רב is so serious that even quoting the רב's own teaching does not excuse it.
steps.confusionAlert: אלעזר did not claim the law as his own idea. He was punished anyway, simply for teaching it in front of משה.

phrases.english: Even though he said to them:
'He commanded my father's brother,'
phrases.notes: Meaning God commanded משה.

phrases.english: 'and He did not command me' —
even so, he was punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: לַאֲחִי אַבָּא צִוָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens רבי אליעזר's proof by ruling out the excuse that אלעזר only quoted משה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even crediting the רב does not permit ruling in his presence. אלעזר was punished regardless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even though אלעזר credited the law to משה, he was still punished for saying it in משה's presence.

steps.title: How אלעזר was lowered: יהושע never needed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows אלעזר's punishment. The תורה said יהושע would stand before אלעזר to ask through the אורים ותומים, but we never find that יהושע needed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall stand before אלעזר הכהן.' But we do not find that יהושע ever needed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the claim from step 40 that אלעזר was 'lowered from his greatness.' It shows what greatness he was promised and how he lost it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in פרשת פינחס gave אלעזר a great honor: יהושע, the leader, would ask him questions through the אורים ותומים. In all of ספר יהושע, we never see יהושע actually do this. So the honor was promised but never used, and that is the 'lowering.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
He shall stand (before someone, to ask him)
The holy item placed in the כהן גדול's breastplate (חושן), through which he asked questions of ה'

steps.confusionAlert: The punishment was not that אלעזר lost the כהונה גדולה. He stayed כהן גדול. He lost the special honor of being consulted by the leader.
steps.whatToRemember: אלעזר ruled in front of משה, so the honor promised to him, that יהושע would consult him, never actually happened.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And before Elazar the priest he shall stand,'
phrases.notes: במדבר כז:כא. Said about יהושע, who would ask through the אורים ותומים.

phrases.english: But we do not find that Joshua needed him.
phrases.notes: Nowhere in תנ״ך does יהושע consult אלעזר's אורים ותומים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 40-41 by showing exactly how אלעזר was 'lowered from his greatness.'
steps.raayaObject: That אלעזר was punished and lowered from his greatness for ruling in front of משה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ולפני אלעזר הכהן יעמד' together with the fact that it is never recorded that יהושע consulted him.

steps.title: רבי לוי: answering in front of one's teacher leads to dying childless
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that whoever answers a word in front of his רב dies without children. His proof is יהושע, who said 'My lord משה, lock them up' in front of משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: Anyone who answers a word in front of his teacher will go down to the grave without a child, as it says: 'And יהושע בן נון, the servant of משה from his youth, answered and said: My lord משה, lock them up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, harsher teaching on the same topic. רבי לוי says that even speaking out of turn in front of your רב carries a heavy punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אלדד ומידד prophesied in the camp, יהושע spoke up before משה could answer and said 'כלאם', meaning 'lock them up.' Because he answered in front of his רב, he was punished by having no children. Notice that רבי לוי's case is broader than רבי אליעזר's. It covers not only ruling a הלכה but even answering a word.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers or replies with a word
The servant and attendant of משה
Lock them up (said about אלדד ומידד)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself does not say יהושע was childless. It only shows that he spoke up in front of משה. The fact that he had no children comes from elsewhere, from the יחוס lists that name no sons of יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows how seriously חז״ל treat a student's respect for his רב. Even a well-meant comment made out of turn is treated as a serious breach.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
Anyone who answers a word in front of his teacher
goes down to the grave without a child,
as it is stated: 'And Joshua son of Nun answered,'
phrases.notes: במדבר יא:כח

phrases.english: the servant of Moses from his youth,
and said: My lord Moses, lock them up.'
phrases.notes: Said about אלדד ומידד, who were prophesying in the camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: כׇּל דְּמוֹתֵיב מִלָּה קַמֵּיהּ רַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second אמורא's teaching on the same theme of speaking before one's רב, with a different and harsher punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who answers a word in the presence of his רב will die childless, as shown by יהושע's 'כלאם' before משה.
